clean_title: Senior Manager — Carbon Markets & Climate Advisory
role_summary: EKI is one of India's larger carbon credit players, and this role leads client engagements from carbon footprint assessments to CCTS readiness. You will manage project delivery, negotiate offset transactions and mentor analysts across multiple projects. The position covers one of the fastest-moving areas in Indian climate policy, the compliance carbon market, so appetite for continuous reading is essential.
key_responsibilities: Lead a portfolio of carbon footprint, offset sourcing and CCTS readiness projects
Structure carbon transactions with rigorous additionality documentation
Own client relationships across manufacturing, energy and agri-processing sectors
Mentor analysts and enforce quality assurance on inventories, projections and registry filings
Track policy developments (CCTS, Article 6) and adjust service offerings accordingly
application_tip: Lead with transaction and delivery numbers: volumes, values, methodologies used, registries navigated. A clear account of one complex deal or filing you carried end to end will do more than a general career summary.

clean_title: Urban Heat & Green Cover Mapping Associate
role_summary: CEPT is building ward-level heat and green cover baselines for Gujarat cities ahead of the next heat season. You will run the geospatial pipeline — LST retrieval, tree crown delineation, change detection — and package results as open dashboards for city engineers. The role suits a GIS analyst who wants municipal-level impact and is comfortable iterating with planners.
key_responsibilities: Produce LST and NDVI/NDBI layers for partner cities using open satellite archives
Delineate tree crowns and green cover with a mix of manual QA and semi-automated methods
Build ward-level dashboards and map atlases for city engineers
Document methods so municipal teams can reproduce the results independently
application_tip: Share a live link or repository for any map or dashboard you have built, even a course project. Reviewers here prefer seeing a reproducible workflow over a portfolio of static PDF maps.

clean_title: GIS & Urban Heat Island Research Associate
organization: WRI India / Climate Centre for Cities
role_summary: Join the team that helps Indian cities plan for extreme heat using satellite data and a lot of patience with municipal records. You will build land surface temperature layers from Landsat and ECOSTRESS imagery, map tree cover across municipal wards, and translate the results into ward-level heat action plans. The role sits between the GIS team and city government partners, so expect a mix of analysis and workshops.
key_responsibilities: Process Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2 imagery to derive land surface temperature (LST) and vegetation indices for partner cities
Map urban tree cover, green cover gaps and heat hotspots at ward level using Google Earth Engine and QGIS
Build and maintain spatial databases of cooling centres, water bodies and shade infrastructure
Prepare data visualisations and fact sheets for city officials and public consultations
Support capacity-building workshops for municipal GIS staff on heat mapping workflows
application_tip: In your cover letter, name one Indian city heat action plan you have read closely and explain what your mapping work would add to it. Concrete dataset choices (why ECOSTRESS over MODIS for a specific analysis) carry more weight than a list of tools.

role_summary: cBalance works with companies, cooperatives and government partners to measure emissions and structure carbon projects across India. As an analyst, you will run GHG inventories against the GHG Protocol, screen carbon offset portfolios, and support BRSR-aligned ESG disclosures for listed clients. Expect roughly half your time on data and half on client meetings and reports.
key_responsibilities: Prepare Scope 1, 2 and 3 greenhouse gas inventories for corporate and institutional clients
Evaluate carbon offset projects (cookstoves, agroforestry, biochar) for additionality and co-benefits
Draft ESG disclosure sections aligned to BRSR Core and GRI standards
Build data collection templates and quality-check client-supplied activity data
Track CCTS and Article 6 developments and brief internal teams on market implications
application_tip: Bring one fully worked example, such as an emissions baseline or a BRSR gap analysis, as a short appendix to your application. Show your unit conversions and assumptions; reviewers check exactly there.

clean_title: Senior Program Officer — Urban Forestry & Afforestation
role_summary: Lead a portfolio of urban forestry and afforestation projects across Uttar Pradesh, from nursery management to five-year survival monitoring. You will work with municipal corporations, forest divisions and community groups to move plantation targets into verified canopy outcomes. This is a senior role for someone who has run field programmes and can handle donors, budgets and government coordination in the same week.
key_responsibilities: Design and implement urban forestry plans for four partner cities in coordination with state forest departments
Oversee nursery operations, species selection and plantation quality audits across project sites
Set up survival-rate and canopy-growth monitoring protocols, including geotagged field data collection
Manage project budgets, donor reporting and compliance for an annual portfolio of ₹4–6 crore
Represent the organisation in state-level CAMPA and Nagar Van Yojana consultations
application_tip: Quantify outcomes you owned rather than activities you attended: hectares planted, survival rates above benchmarks, species mix, nursery throughput. A reference who can speak to your government coordination will help your case.

organization: Anna University — Centre for Climate Change & Adaptation Research
role_summary: The Centre for Climate Change and Adaptation Research works on coastal city adaptation, monsoon variability and heat-health early warning systems in Tamil Nadu. As a specialist, you will lead vulnerability assessments, contribute to state climate action updates, and anchor a small team of analysts and interns. You will also be the bridge between model outputs and what district officials can actually use.
key_responsibilities: Lead city-level climate vulnerability and risk assessments for coastal Tamil Nadu
Translate downscaled climate projections into ward and sector-level risk maps
Support preparation and revision of state and city climate action plans
Supervise analysts and interns and set quality standards for data and deliverables
Publish findings in journals and present at state technical committees
application_tip: Show one deliverable that made it into a government process, such as a plan chapter, a committee note or a budget line. Be explicit about modelling choices as well; reviewers here care about how you communicate uncertainty, not only the model you used.

organization: ATREE (Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment)
role_summary: ATREE seeks a research associate for its climate adaptation programme working at the intersection of forests, water and farming landscapes in the Western Ghats. You will collect and analyse field data, support participatory research with local communities, and contribute to peer-reviewed publications. Fieldwork blocks of two to three weeks are part of the job, not an exception.
key_responsibilities: Collect ecological and socio-economic data across study landscapes in Karnataka and Kerala
Clean, analyse and document datasets in R or Python following reproducible workflows
Support participatory mapping and focus group discussions with community institutions
Co-author research papers, policy briefs and donor reports
Coordinate field logistics, research permits and data-sharing agreements
application_tip: Attach a writing sample and describe a dataset you cleaned yourself. The strongest applicants explain how they handled messy field data — missing values, inconsistent plots, GPS drift — not just the final results.

clean_title: Junior Research Fellow — Urban Forest Carbon & Canopy Mapping
role_summary: The Forest Research Institute is inviting Junior Research Fellows to support a study on carbon sequestration and canopy structure in urban and peri-urban forests. You will assist with plot-level measurements, allometric modelling and remote sensing validation across Dehradun and neighbouring districts. The fellowship suits a recent postgraduate preparing for research or a specialisation in forestry and remote sensing.
key_responsibilities: Lay out and measure permanent sampling plots; record DBH, height and species data
Process drone and satellite imagery to validate canopy cover estimates
Maintain carbon stock datasets and support allometric model development
Help prepare progress reports for the sponsor and conference abstracts
application_tip: State your NET, GATE or equivalent credentials in the first paragraph, since shortlisting weighs them heavily. If your dissertation involved field plots or imagery, summarise it in three sentences with numbers.

role_summary: FES works on commons governance, forests, pastures and water bodies, with village institutions across eight Indian states. This fellowship places early-career researchers with field teams for eighteen months, combining policy analysis with lived practice. Fellows spend significant time at field locations and contribute to both village-level agreements and state-level policy notes.
key_responsibilities: Document commons governance arrangements and their environmental outcomes across partner states
Support policy analysis on forest rights, FRA implementation and commons-linked schemes
Facilitate workshops with village institutions and panchayats
Produce field notes, case studies and policy commentary
Maintain data records for long-term monitoring studies
must_have_skills: Hindi plus one regional language (working proficiency)
application_tip: The fellowship values demonstrated field time over academic pedigree. Mention concrete village or community-level work, and be honest about your language range, because field placements are matched to it.

clean_title: Policy Research Fellow — Urban Green Infrastructure
role_summary: A twelve-month policy fellowship hosted at IIFM, working with the Madhya Pradesh forest department on urban green infrastructure, from Nagar Van site reviews to state-level mission documentation. Fellows review schemes, run stakeholder interviews and produce briefs that feed directly into budget and planning notes. This is a writing-heavy role with structured mentoring from faculty and departmental officers.
key_responsibilities: Review central and state schemes (Nagar Van Yojana, CAMPA, Smart Cities) for alignment with urban green infrastructure goals
Conduct stakeholder interviews with municipal and forest officials across five to six cities
Draft policy briefs, budget notes and implementation checklists
Maintain a documented evidence base with sources for every claim in the briefs
application_tip: Send one short policy brief of two to three pages on any urban environmental scheme you have studied. Fellowship panels almost always ask what you wrote and who used it, so have a specific answer ready.
